main.label: Neuralink · >50,000 accumulated recording hours
main.sourceTitle: Neuralink · >50,000 accumulated recording hours — primary source
main.quote: In the two years since our clinical trial began, our participants have streamed over 50,000 hours of unlabeled, freeform neural data.
main.note: Company-reported accumulated unlabeled freeform neural recording duration from human trial participants. Live-use results use participant-specific encoders pretrained on thousands of hours each. Formal session-union, gap and quality-control rules, contributor count and public access remain unspecified. The first participant's >9,000 hours is a subset of the disclosed total.

recordingCoverage.detail: The contributor count for >50,000 h is undisclosed. Trial enrollment and the six participants in the performance analysis describe different populations. The first participant’s >9,000 h is part of the total; other per-person durations are unspecified.

main.label: AJILE12 frozen release
main.quote: Neural recordings are available at 500 Hz from at least 64 electrodes per participant, for a total of 1280 hours.
main.note: Release metadata: “Neural recordings are available at 500 Hz from at least 64 electrodes per participant, for a total of 1280 hours.” Published January 27, 2022. Duration counts recording time once across electrodes; gaps and preprocessing affect quality-valid hours.

recordingCoverage.detail: DANDI 000055/0.220127.0436 reports 12 subjects and 1,280 h. The descriptor gives 3–5 recording days per participant and 55 semi-continuous days total. Exact session counts and quality-valid hour ranges are unspecified.

supportingReferences.title: AJILE12 Scientific Data descriptor · 3–5 recording days per participant

main.label: POYO-1 training corpus
main.note: Abstract: “over 100 hours of recordings” from seven nonhuman primates and over 158 sessions. The strict lower bound describes existing recordings reused for training; access varies by constituent dataset.

recordingCoverage.detail: The paper’s >100 h training corpus spans seven nonhuman primates and >158 sessions. Existing recordings are reused; constituent access varies. Typical session length and the distribution of per-animal durations remain unspecified.

main.label: JapanEEG descriptor
main.quote: 1020 hours of simultaneously recorded scalp electroencephalography (EEG), facial electromyography (EMG), and speech audio from three healthy native Japanese speakers
main.note: Abstract: “1020 hours of simultaneously recorded scalp electroencephalography (EEG), facial electromyography (EMG), and speech audio”. In descriptor v2 (November 17, 2026), authors report controlled access through Harvard Dataverse, with voice-masked audio. The point retains initial descriptor submission timing; archive upload timing remains unverified. Version 2 adds current access and duration evidence. Duration counts simultaneous modalities once; the released file inventory remains unverified.

recordingCoverage.detail: Calculated from descriptor v2 Table 4 recording-hour cells: P01 ≈813.8 h, P02 ≈146.2 h, P03 ≈60.3 h. Shared covert-repetition/listening recordings are counted once. Rounded cells sum to 1,020.3 h versus Table 3’s 1,020.4 h; the plotted abstract total stays 1,020 h. Per-person durations accumulate across recordings; the displayed range is calculated from these cells.

supportingReferences.title: JapanEEG descriptor v2 · November 17, 2026 · Tables 3–4 and Data Records

main.group: JapanEEG · human scalp EEG, controlled access

main.label: BrainGate T15 · independent speech and cursor BCI use
main.sourceTitle: Card et al. (2026) · Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain–computer interface for speech and cursor control
main.sourceRole: Reported BCI-use duration and recording/access methods
main.quote: As of 22.6 months after the implant surgery, he had accumulated more than 3,800 h of BCI use
main.note: Card et al. report >3,800 h of BCI use by participant T15. The plotted ≈3,800 h uses BCI-use time as an approximate recording-duration basis across speech and cursor operation. Methods state that session data were saved except during privacy mode; the exact retained recording duration is unspecified. Independent-use neural data and speech transcripts are withheld for participant privacy; figure and statistical summaries are public. Dated to June 15, 2026 publication.

recordingCoverage.detail: Participant T15 is the single human contributor to the reported >3,800 h of BCI use. The plotted ≈3,800 h is an approximate recording duration across speech and cursor operation. Session data were saved except during privacy mode; the exact retained recording duration is unspecified. Session counts matched to retained recordings are unreported.

supportingReferences.title: Card et al. · figure and statistical reproduction data
